Samir — thanks. A couple of technical clarifications before we commit to the higher-throughput tier: 
1) Does the higher tier guarantee KV cache persistence across warm restarts? We rely on stable prefix caching for chat workloads.
2) What is the per-request payload size limit and maximum sequence length supported? Our current tail workloads occasionally hit 8k tokens.
3) Any imposed rate limits per API key vs per-account? We run sharded clients and want to avoid throttling when spikes come from a single key.

If you can include these details in the SOW/appendix, that will speed our legal/ops review. Also, SLA needed for latency targets — can you share the SLA table for both tiers (monthly uptime and 95th/99th latency bounds)?

Thanks — Vivek
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@finsight.io>

Subject: Re: FinSight renewal + proposed SOW and usage model

Vivek — answers below and I attached an SLA table as Appendix D in the updated SOW Word doc (I'll send the editable file right after this).

1) KV cache persistence: higher-throughput nodes provide sticky cache buckets for warm restarts — we guarantee cache persistence across rolling restarts within a single AZ. Cross-AZ sticky caching is an add-on; noted in Appendix C.
2) Payload/sequence length: we support up to 12k token sequences on the higher-throughput tier; default tier is 4k. There is a pricing delta when enabling >8k token support due to memory footprint.
3) Rate limits: rate-limits are enforced at the API-key level by default; enterprise accounts can request account-level rate shaping to avoid per-key throttles. We'll include the config options and recommended request patterns in the integration guide.

Next steps I suggest:
- I'll upload the editable SOW and SLA appendix by EOD Tue 3/17.
- Marissa: once you confirm procurement window (target 3/18 review), I'll lock pricing for 90 days.
- Neha: I'll send the SOC 2 summary and a pointer to the subprocessors list for your review; sign an NDA if you need the full report.

If that works, I can schedule a 30-min technical call (Mon 3/16 at 10:00 PT) — looks like that landed before your reply so if you'd still like it, we can reschedule.

Best,
Samir
